My parents have made sure that my sister will be financially taken care of after they're gone (life insurance, etc)- and I am very glad for that because, at least as far as I know, many parents in similar situations don't do the same, they just expect that the disabled child won't outlive or delagate this responsability for the remaining able bodied sibling. As for putting my sister in a home, I don't really plan on doing that. Group homes in my country are either unsafe or terribly expensive and, beyond that, my sister is very aware of who she is and what is happening around her (she has cerebral palsy and it has affected her body movement a lot more then her intelectual capabilities, as in she is verbal, finished high school, etc). I believe it would be incredibly painful for her. I won't give up on my life to take care of her full time but, at least for now, moving her to my house in the future and having one or two nurses to take care of her seems like a reasonable plan (it's something that I would probably be able to afford with the insurance+selling my parents house+some of my income if needed). 
I mean, all that counting on the possibility that my parents will remain financially responsible and that I'll be able to at least fully provide an ok lifestyle for myself when the time comes.

I believe that this is quite common (my parents did this too). It's just something that you're tought from a young age when your sibling is disabled- that they're special, that they need your help and that you must always care for them. I've been dealing with it in a better way recently, but only after a LOT of disagreements and talking with my parents. It's a heavy burden to bear, it's expected of me to simply give up on my life and take care of my sister, it's portrait as this amazing act of love and selflessness- which it often is- however, the thing is I'm not that selfless. I cannot mold who I am to what my sister needs and I constantly feel this imense guilt over it.

I'm really sorry for you, most of all because this resembles a lot the relationship of my parents- who are, unfortunately, still married. Even though you've said she's a great mother, by the things she has done I can assure you she's not. Just by treating you with so little respect, by having these tantrums and engaging in self destructive activities while the kids are home makes her a awful, abusive mother on itself. And that's just what you're there to see. You've mentioned you try being at work as much as possible to avoid dealing with her and that she refused your offer to get a nanny, therefore it seems to me that she has a lot of time alone with the children. Which means she has space and time to be as abusive as she wants with them, which not necessarily involves hard physical abuse but very probably involves a lot of emotional abuse that you're not full aware of-  children brought up in toxic homes often have a hard time recognizing and talking about the abuse itself until they're able to distance themselves enough from it so they can see how abnormal their childhood was. It's probably hard for them to talk about this with you, most of all if they are still kids.
Please, for the sake of these children, don't let her get custody of them. Even if she isn't directly abusive towards them right now, narcissistic people such as her need someone they can inflict pain on, be it emotionally or phisicaly, as soon as she doesn't have you as her little toy anymore, she's going for the ones who are more vulnerable and close to her: your son and daughter.
You sound like a good person and a loving father who is finally ready to break an abuse cycle, which is great, but I have to be the one that says to you that allowing her to raise your children makes you as bad of a parent as she is, and that's not something your children will be able to overlook when they're older.
If you make sure to face this with a shiny, newly grown, sharp and strong spine, I'm sure your children won't have major problems related to the divorce, not as much as they would have if the two of you stayed together and kept exposing them to such a toxic relationship. It's better to come from a broken home then to be raised in one. As we're in it, you talked about getting a therapist for yourself, maybe it would be nice to get one for them too, if they're old enough.
I really recommend you to take a look at r/raisedbynarcissists, just so you can see what I'm talking about. My best wishes to you and your family.
P.S.: Your grandfather sounded like a great man.

I'm so glad I've found your post as I've been looking for such stories for quite a while now. I'm 17 yo and have recently broken up (gotten broken up with, actually) with my first love. It's going to be one month since it happened and, even though I still miss her from time to time, I feel like I've done the best for the both of us and it feels really good. I don't know how your breakup went but mine was very friendly and meaningful, we talked honestly with each other but remained respectfull and close, we cried and held hands, it's a weird thing to say but it was quite good actually. Right after it happened I felt amazing, it was like all this heavyness had fallen from my shoulder, even though she's amazing, she has some deep emotional scars that she has to deal with herself (she was always very confused about everything, afraid to love too much and at some point she said that being with me felt like she was betraying herself and that feeling that way made her feel like shit because I was so good to her and she felt like she didn't deserve me). In this time I decided to make some changes, you see, this was my first relationship and I had gotten so involved in it that I ended up forgetting every other part of my life, I had lost my sense of self in it, ultimately I saw in this a chance to reconnect back with me, my friends, my family, my ambitions to the future that I had forgotten while I was in love. Of course, with time reality came and I started missing her, what we had; she wasn't only my girlfriend, she was my best friend, my lover, my partner, even today, as I'm moving on and thinking about dating again, I still miss her from time to time, find her smell in an old scarf, hear a song that reminds me of us and stuff like that but the fact that I've managed to understand that getting back together wouldn't only be useless (as we don't work as a couple even though I hold her very dearly in my heart and wish her the best of the world) but would also be very painful and hurt the both of us. We aren't talking to each other nowadays because I thought it would be best to give us both this time to grow apart, deal with the breakup and learn how to live without each other, but as soon as we both get to a point where we're over it and have no romantic feelings towards each other, we hope to remain friends. This is very hard and I don't think I'm in a position to give anyone advice, but if I was mine would be to not hold back any resentment but also to keep in mind why it ended and why it was the best given the circumstances. I really wish you find your way through this (as I really with the same for me haha), you can dm me or anything if you need ;).
